ts1_defined.topic: Definitions of Christian Zionism; the term 'theology shield' in this series and this volume; the Prejean Boller case as an example of the second meaning

claims.text: Britannica defines Christian Zionism as 'a religious and political Christian movement that supports the return of the Jewish Diaspora to a homeland in Palestine as a prerequisite for the end-time' (article by Frannie Comstock).

Samuel Goldman's God's Country (University of Pennsylvania Press, 2018) is described by its publisher as telling the story of Christian Zionism 'from the Puritans to 9/11' and names three sources of American Christian support for a Jewish state: covenant, prophecy and cultural affinity.

Keith Mathison (Ligonier, 2 Feb 2022): dispensationalism 'at its heart is the distinction between Israel and the church'; it began with John Nelson Darby in the 19th century, spread through the Bible Conference movement and the Scofield Reference Bible (1909); covenant theology 'affirms that there is one people of God' and 'Paul defines Abraham's seed in terms of Jesus Christ'.

CUFI was founded in 2006 by John Hagee; it claimed over seven million members by 2019 and over ten million by 2023 (self-reported). Hagee: 'We believe in the promise of Genesis 12:3 regarding the Jewish people and the nation of Israel', 'an eternal covenant between God and the seed of Abraham'; JVL reports Hagee's statement that support is not aimed at converting Jews and is owed as 'a debt of gratitude to the Jewish people'. Statement undated on the page.

Pew Research Center (Lipka, 3 Oct 2013): 82% of white evangelical Protestants said God gave the land of Israel to the Jewish people, compared with 40% of American Jews (55% of Jews who believe in God).

Holy See Commission for Religious Relations with the Jews, Notes (1985), section VI: Christians are asked to understand Jewish 'religious attachment which finds its roots in biblical tradition' without adopting 'any particular religious interpretation of this relationship'; 'The existence of the State of Israel and its political options should be envisaged not in a perspective which is in itself religious' but in reference to 'the common principles of international law'.

At a White House Religious Liberty Commission hearing on antisemitism (Monday 9 Feb 2026), commissioner Carrie Prejean Boller told Rabbi Ari Berman: 'I'm a Catholic and Catholics do not embrace Zionism. Just so you know.' Chair Dan Patrick (Texas Lt. Gov.) removed her, writing on X that 'No member of the Commission has the right to hijack a hearing for their own personal and political agenda on any issue'; she refused to resign and wrote that she 'will never bend the knee to the state of Israel'.

Jewish Insider reported that Prejean Boller asked the Jewish witnesses 'So are all Catholics antisemites?', pressed them on whether they would consider her antisemitic for believing Jews killed Jesus, and had defended Candace Owens; Patrick said the removal 'was my decision'; the White House did not comment.

ts1_genesis.topic: Genesis 12:3: text; the reading applied to the Jewish people and the modern state; the reading fulfilled in Christ and the church; who holds each

claims.text: Genesis 12:3 KJV: 'And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.' NIV: 'I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.' ESV renders the curse clause 'him who dishonors you I will curse'.
Galatians 3:16 KJV: 'Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.'

Scofield's 1917 note summarising the Abrahamic Covenant (at Gen 15:18): on 'And curse him that curseth thee': 'Wonderfully fulfilled in the history of the dispersion. It has invariably fared ill with the people who have persecuted the Jew -- well with those who have protected him. The future will still more remarkably prove this principle'; on 'In thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed': 'This is the great evangelic promise fulfilled in Abraham's Seed, Christ'; the 'great nation' clause has a threefold fulfilment (natural seed, spiritual seed of faith, Ishmael); 'The gift of the land is modified by prophecies of three dispossessions and restorations', with Israel now in the third dispersion, to be restored at the Lord's return. The wording 'protected him' corrects the leads' 'protected it'.
Scofield's 1917 note at Gen 12:1 calls the Abrahamic Covenant 'wholly gracious and unconditional' and dates the Dispensation of Promise from Gen 12:1 to Exod 19:8.

Bruce N. Fisk (Network of Evangelicals for the Middle East), Bibliotheca Sacra April–June 2023: 'Genesis 12:3 often serves as warrant for standing with Israel and blessing the Jewish people'; traces the reading through Shaftesbury and Blackstone (1891) and quotes Scofield; poses questions including whether God promised to bless the modern state of Israel; first presented at the Evangelical Theological Society, 2021.

Sen. Ted Cruz in a Tucker Carlson interview posted 18 June 2025: 'As a Christian, growing up in Sunday school, I was taught from the Bible that those who bless Israel will be blessed'; 'I want to be on the blessing side of things'; 'it doesn't say the government of, it says the nation of Israel'. Carlson: 'Those who bless the government of Israel?'; 'You're saying as a Christian, if I believe in Jesus, I have to support the modern state of Israel?' Former ambassador David Friedman on X: 'This is the same nation of Israel referred to in the Bible'.
Catechism of the Catholic Church 121: the books of the Old Testament 'retain a permanent value, for the Old Covenant has never been revoked'.

Church of Scotland Church and Society report 'The Inheritance of Abraham? A report on the promised land' (2013) called on the Church to 'refute claims that scripture offers any peoples a privileged claim for possession of a particular territory'; a revised version issued 17 May 2013; SCoJeC called it 'an outrage to everything that interfaith dialogue stands for', the Board of Deputies 'deeply troubling', Rabbi David Rosen (AJC) 'rather pathetic'.

Jerusalem Declaration on Christian Zionism, 22 Aug 2006, signed by Latin Patriarch Michel Sabbah, Syriac Orthodox Archbishop Swerios Malki Mourad, Anglican Bishop Riah Abu El-Assal and Lutheran Bishop Munib Younan: calls Christian Zionism a 'false teaching that corrupts the biblical message of love, justice, and reconciliation'. A response signed by representatives of ICEJ, Bridges for Peace and Christian Friends of Israel denied it is a heresy, grounded its position in the Bible including God's gift of the land, and called Christian Zionism 'not a threat to anybody, but instead seeks to be a blessing'.

PC(USA): the 226th General Assembly (2024) adopted an overture 'On Confessing our Complicity in Christian Zionism'; Ray Jones III said it called for 'rejecting Christian Zionism in all its forms'; a gathering 'Christianity without Christian Zionism' was held 6–8 Aug 2026 in Louisville.
